newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to buy gas, electricity from Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to buy gas, electricity from Turkmenistan.

text.p: Turkey will import natural gas and electricity from the former Soviet republic of Turkmenistan as part of efforts to diversify energy resources and help close power deficits, officials said on Friday.
"The agreement for gas and electricity purchases was signed in Ashgabat by our energy minister and Turkmen officials," an energy official told Reuters.

He said Energy Minister Recai Kutan, who returned from Turkmenistan on Thursday, had signed the deal to initially buy three billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas from 1999 and electric power through an existing grid to Turkey via Iran.
"Turkmen natural gas will be some 30 percent cheaper than other purchases we make," said the official, who declined to be identified.
Turkey buys a total of about nine bmc of natural gas annually from Russia, Algeria and spot markets.
It struck a 25-year, $13.5 billion deal earlier in the week with Russia's gas giant Gazprom to get gas reaching 30 bcm annually by 2010 through another pipeline network.
Its plans to get three bmc of Iranian gas under a 23-year, $23-billion deal from 1998 is underway. Supplies from Iran will rise to 10 bcm by 2005, which include seven bcm of Turkmen gas.

The official said Turkmen gas will be pumped out to Turkey on an existing pipeline from Turkmenistan to Iran's Tabriz. Turkey and Iran will soon begin building the first phase of a 1,420-km (890-mile) line from Tabriz to Ankara.
He said gas from Turkmenistan, which has the second largest gas reserves of 21 trillion bcm in the world after Russia, would futurely be transported to Europe through Turkey.
"Turkmen gas supplies will evetually reach up to 30 bcm. We have agreed with Turkmens to supply gas to Europe through a company that will market the gas," he said.
"Work to form the company, which will have foreign partners, will begin in two months," he said.
Turkey will also receive electricity from Turkmenistan through an existing 132-kilovolt (KV) grid passing Iran and 154-KV lines in Turkey, he said, but did not say when purchases would begin.
"Another line of 400 KV capacity will be built to get more electricity from Turkmenistan," he said.
Turkey, which has an electricity shortage of 2.5 billion kiloWatt-hours, has begun buying power from Iran, Georgia and Bulgaria.
